lines.text: Flourish of trumpets, then hautboys. Enter the King, Gloucester, Salisbury, Warwick, and Cardinal Beaufort on the one side; the Queen, Suffolk, York, Somerset and Buckingham on the other.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As by your high imperial Majesty

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I had in charge at my depart for France,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As procurator to your excellence,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To marry Princess Margaret for your grace,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So, in the famous ancient city Tours,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: In presence of the Kings of France and Sicil,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The Dukes of Orleans, Calaber, Bretagne, and Alençon,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Seven earls, twelve barons, and twenty reverend bishops,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I have performed my task and was espoused,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And humbly now upon my bended knee,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: In sight of England and her lordly peers,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Deliver up my title in the Queen

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To your most gracious hands, that are the substance

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Of that great shadow I did represent:

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The happiest gift that ever marquess gave,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The fairest queen that ever king received.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Suffolk, arise.—Welcome, Queen Margaret.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I can express no kinder sign of love

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than this kind kiss.—O Lord, that lends me life,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lend me a heart replete with thankfulness!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For Thou hast given me in this beauteous face

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A world of earthly blessings to my soul,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If sympathy of love unite our thoughts.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Great King of England and my gracious lord,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The mutual conference that my mind hath had

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: By day, by night, waking and in my dreams,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: In courtly company or at my beads,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: With you, mine alderliefest sovereign,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Makes me the bolder to salute my King

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: With ruder terms, such as my wit affords

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And overjoy of heart doth minister.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Her sight did ravish, but her grace in speech,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Her words yclad with wisdom’s majesty,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Makes me from wondering fall to weeping joys,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Such is the fulness of my heart’s content.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lords, with one cheerful voice welcome my love.
[_Kneeling_.]

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Long live Queen Margaret, England’s happiness!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: We thank you all.
[_Flourish._]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: My Lord Protector, so it please your grace,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Here are the articles of contracted peace

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Between our sovereign and the French king Charles,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: For eighteen months concluded by consent.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Imprimis, _it is agreed between the French king Charles and

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: William de la Pole, Marquess of Suffolk, ambassador for Henry, King of

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: England, that the said Henry shall espouse the Lady Margaret, daughter

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: unto Reignier King of Naples, Sicilia, and Jerusalem, and crown her

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Queen of England ere the thirtieth of May next ensuing._ Item, _that

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: the duchy of Anjou and the county of Maine shall be released and

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: delivered to the King her father_—
[_Lets the paper fall._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Uncle, how now?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Pardon me, gracious lord.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Some sudden qualm hath struck me at the heart

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And dimmed mine eyes, that I can read no further.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Uncle of Winchester, I pray read on.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Item, _it is further agreed between them, that the duchies

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: of Anjou and Maine shall be released and delivered to the King her

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: father, and she sent over of the King of England’s own proper cost and

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: charges, without having any dowry._

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: They please us well.—Lord Marquess, kneel down.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We here create thee the first Duke of Suffolk,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And girt thee with the sword.—Cousin of York,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We here discharge your grace from being regent

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I’ th’ parts of France, till term of eighteen months

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be full expired.—Thanks, uncle Winchester,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Gloucester, York, Buckingham, Somerset,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Salisbury, and Warwick;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We thank you all for this great favour done

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: In entertainment to my princely Queen.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come, let us in, and with all speed provide

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To see her coronation be performed.
[_Exeunt King, Queen and Suffolk._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Brave peers of England, pillars of the state,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To you Duke Humphrey must unload his grief,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Your grief, the common grief of all the land.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What! Did my brother Henry spend his youth,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: His valour, coin, and people, in the wars?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Did he so often lodge in open field,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: In winter’s cold and summer’s parching heat,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To conquer France, his true inheritance?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And did my brother Bedford toil his wits

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To keep by policy what Henry got?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Have you yourselves, Somerset, Buckingham,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Brave York, Salisbury, and victorious Warwick,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Received deep scars in France and Normandy?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Or hath mine uncle Beaufort and myself,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: With all the learned council of the realm,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Studied so long, sat in the council house

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Early and late, debating to and fro

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: How France and Frenchmen might be kept in awe,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And had his highness in his infancy

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Crowned in Paris in despite of foes?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And shall these labours and these honours die?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Shall Henry’s conquest, Bedford’s vigilance,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Your deeds of war, and all our counsel die?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: O peers of England, shameful is this league!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Fatal this marriage, cancelling your fame,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Blotting your names from books of memory,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Razing the characters of your renown,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Defacing monuments of conquered France,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Undoing all, as all had never been!

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Nephew, what means this passionate discourse,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: This peroration with such circumstance?

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: For France, ’tis ours; and we will keep it still.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Ay, uncle, we will keep it if we can,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But now it is impossible we should.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Suffolk, the new-made duke that rules the roast,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Hath given the duchy of Anjou and Maine

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Unto the poor King Reignier, whose large style

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Agrees not with the leanness of his purse.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Now, by the death of Him that died for all,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: These counties were the keys of Normandy!

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: But wherefore weeps Warwick, my valiant son?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For grief that they are past recovery;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For, were there hope to conquer them again,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My sword should shed hot blood, mine eyes no tears.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Anjou and Maine! Myself did win them both,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Those provinces these arms of mine did conquer;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And are the cities that I got with wounds

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Delivered up again with peaceful words?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: _Mort Dieu!_

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For Suffolk’s duke, may he be suffocate,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That dims the honour of this warlike isle!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: France should have torn and rent my very heart

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Before I would have yielded to this league.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I never read but England’s kings have had

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Large sums of gold and dowries with their wives;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And our King Henry gives away his own,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To match with her that brings no vantages.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: A proper jest, and never heard before,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That Suffolk should demand a whole fifteenth

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: For costs and charges in transporting her!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: She should have staid in France, and starved in France,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Before—

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: My Lord of Gloucester, now ye grow too hot.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: It was the pleasure of my lord the King.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: My Lord of Winchester, I know your mind.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: ’Tis not my speeches that you do mislike,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But ’tis my presence that doth trouble ye.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Rancour will out. Proud prelate, in thy face

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I see thy fury. If I longer stay,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: We shall begin our ancient bickerings.—

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Lordings, farewell; and say, when I am gone,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I prophesied France will be lost ere long.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: So, there goes our Protector in a rage.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: ’Tis known to you he is mine enemy,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Nay, more, an enemy unto you all,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: And no great friend, I fear me, to the King.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Consider, lords, he is the next of blood

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: And heir apparent to the English crown.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Had Henry got an empire by his marriage,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: And all the wealthy kingdoms of the west,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: There’s reason he should be displeased at it.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Look to it, lords. Let not his smoothing words

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Bewitch your hearts; be wise and circumspect.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: What though the common people favour him,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Calling him “Humphrey, the good Duke of Gloucester,”

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Clapping their hands, and crying with loud voice,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: “Jesu maintain your royal excellence!”

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: With “God preserve the good Duke Humphrey!”

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: I fear me, lords, for all this flattering gloss,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: He will be found a dangerous Protector.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Why should he, then, protect our sovereign,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: He being of age to govern of himself?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Cousin of Somerset, join you with me,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And all together, with the Duke of Suffolk,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: We’ll quickly hoist Duke Humphrey from his seat.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: This weighty business will not brook delay;

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: I’ll to the Duke of Suffolk presently.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Cousin of Buckingham, though Humphrey’s pride

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And greatness of his place be grief to us,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Yet let us watch the haughty cardinal;

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: His insolence is more intolerable

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Than all the princes’ in the land beside.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: If Gloucester be displaced, he’ll be Protector.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Or thou or I, Somerset, will be Protector,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Despite Duke Humphrey or the Cardinal.
[_Exeunt Buckingham and Somerset._]

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Pride went before; 	Ambition follows him.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: While these do labour for their own preferment,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Behoves it us to labour for the realm.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: I never saw but Humphrey Duke of Gloucester,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Did bear him like a noble gentleman.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Oft have I seen the haughty Cardinal,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: More like a soldier than a man o’ th’ church,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: As stout and proud as he were lord of all,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Swear like a ruffian and demean himself

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Unlike the ruler of a commonweal.—

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Warwick my son, the comfort of my age,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Thy deeds, thy plainness, and thy housekeeping,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Hath won the greatest favour of the commons,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Excepting none but good Duke Humphrey.—

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And, brother York, thy acts in Ireland,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: In bringing them to civil discipline,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Thy late exploits done in the heart of France,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: When thou wert regent for our sovereign,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Have made thee feared and honoured of the people.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Join we together for the public good,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: In what we can to bridle and suppress

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: The pride of Suffolk and the Cardinal,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: With Somerset’s and Buckingham’s ambition;

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And, as we may, cherish Duke Humphrey’s deeds

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: While they do tend the profit of the land.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: So God help Warwick, as he loves the land

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And common profit of his country!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And so says York, [_Aside_.] for he hath greatest cause.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Then let’s make haste away and look unto the main.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Unto the main! O father, Maine is lost,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That Maine which by main force Warwick did win,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And would have kept so long as breath did last!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Main chance, father, you meant; but I meant Maine,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Which I will win from France, or else be slain.
[_Exeunt Warwick and Salisbury._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Anjou and Maine are given to the French;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Paris is lost; the state of Normandy

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Stands on a tickle point now they are gone.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Suffolk concluded on the articles,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The peers agreed, and Henry was well pleased

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To change two dukedoms for a duke’s fair daughter.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I cannot blame them all. What is’t to them?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: ’Tis thine they give away, and not their own.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Pirates may make cheap pennyworths of their pillage,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And purchase friends, and give to courtesans,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Still revelling like lords till all be gone;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whileas the silly owner of the goods

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Weeps over them, and wrings his hapless hands,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And shakes his head, and trembling stands aloof,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: While all is shared and all is borne away,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Ready to starve and dare not touch his own.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So York must sit and fret and bite his tongue,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: While his own lands are bargained for and sold.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Methinks the realms of England, France, and Ireland

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Bear that proportion to my flesh and blood

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: As did the fatal brand Althaea burnt

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Unto the prince’s heart of Calydon.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Anjou and Maine both given unto the French!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Cold news for me, for I had hope of France,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Even as I have of fertile England’s soil.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: A day will come when York shall claim his own;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And therefore I will take the Nevilles’ parts,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And make a show of love to proud Duke Humphrey,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And when I spy advantage, claim the crown,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For that’s the golden mark I seek to hit.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Nor shall proud Lancaster usurp my right,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Nor hold the sceptre in his childish fist,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Nor wear the diadem upon his head,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whose church-like humours fits not for a crown.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then, York, be still awhile till time do serve.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Watch thou and wake when others be asleep,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To pry into the secrets of the state;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Till Henry, surfeiting in joys of love

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: With his new bride and England’s dear-bought Queen,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And Humphrey with the peers be fallen at jars.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then will I raise aloft the milk-white rose,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: With whose sweet smell the air shall be perfumed,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And in my standard bear the arms of York,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To grapple with the house of Lancaster;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And force perforce I’ll make him yield the crown,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whose bookish rule hath pulled fair England down.
[_Exit._]
Enter Duke Humphrey of Gloucester and his wife Eleanor.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Why droops my lord, like over-ripened corn

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Hanging the head at Ceres’ plenteous load?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Why doth the great Duke Humphrey knit his brows,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: As frowning at the favours of the world?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Why are thine eyes fixed to the sullen earth,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Gazing on that which seems to dim thy sight?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: What seest thou there? King Henry’s diadem,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Enchased with all the honours of the world?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: If so, gaze on, and grovel on thy face,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Until thy head be circled with the same.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Put forth thy hand, reach at the glorious gold.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: What, is’t too short? I’ll lengthen it with mine;

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And, having both together heaved it up,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: We’ll both together lift our heads to heaven,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And never more abase our sight so low

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: As to vouchsafe one glance unto the ground.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: O Nell, sweet Nell, if thou dost love thy lord,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Banish the canker of ambitious thoughts.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And may that hour when I imagine ill

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Against my King and nephew, virtuous Henry,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Be my last breathing in this mortal world!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: My troublous dreams this night doth make me sad.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: What dreamed my lord? Tell me, and I’ll requite it

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: With sweet rehearsal of my morning’s dream.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Methought this staff, mine office-badge in court,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Was broke in twain; by whom I have forgot,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But, as I think, it was by th’ Cardinal,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And on the pieces of the broken wand

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Were placed the heads of Edmund, Duke of Somerset

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And William de la Pole, first Duke of Suffolk.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: This was my dream; what it doth bode, God knows.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Tut, this was nothing but an argument

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: That he that breaks a stick of Gloucester’s grove

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Shall lose his head for his presumption.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: But list to me, my Humphrey, my sweet Duke:

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Methought I sat in seat of majesty

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: In the cathedral church of Westminster

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And in that chair where kings and queens are crowned,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Where Henry and Dame Margaret kneeled to me

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And on my head did set the diadem.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Nay, Eleanor, then must I chide outright.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Presumptuous dame, ill-nurtured Eleanor,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Art thou not second woman in the realm,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And the Protector’s wife, beloved of him?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Hast thou not worldly pleasure at command,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Above the reach or compass of thy thought?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And wilt thou still be hammering treachery

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To tumble down thy husband and thyself

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: From top of honour to disgrace’s feet?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Away from me, and let me hear no more!

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: What, what, my lord! Are you so choleric

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: With Eleanor for telling but her dream?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Next time I’ll keep my dreams unto myself,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And not be checked.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Nay, be not angry, I am pleased again.
Enter Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My Lord Protector, ’tis his highness’ pleasure

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: You do prepare to ride unto Saint Albans,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Whereas the King and Queen do mean to hawk.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I go. Come, Nell, thou wilt ride with us?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Yes, my good lord, I’ll follow presently.
[_Exeunt Gloucester and Messenger._]

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Follow I must; I cannot go before

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: While Gloucester bears this base and humble mind.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Were I a man, a duke, and next of blood,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: I would remove these tedious stumbling-blocks

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And smooth my way upon their headless necks;

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And, being a woman, I will not be slack

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: To play my part in Fortune’s pageant.—

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Where are you there? Sir John! Nay, fear not, man,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: We are alone; here’s none but thee and I.
Enter Hume.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Jesus preserve your royal majesty!

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: What sayst thou? Majesty! I am but grace.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: But, by the grace of God, and Hume’s advice,

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Your grace’s title shall be multiplied.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: What sayst thou, man? Hast thou as yet conferred

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: With Margery Jourdain, the cunning witch,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: With Roger Bolingbroke, the conjurer?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And will they undertake to do me good?

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: This they have promised, to show your highness

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: A spirit raised from depth of underground,

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: That shall make answer to such questions

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: As by your Grace shall be propounded him.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: It is enough, I’ll think upon the questions.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: When from Saint Albans we do make return,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: We’ll see these things effected to the full.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Here, Hume, take this reward; make merry, man,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: With thy confederates in this weighty cause.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Hume must make merry with the Duchess’ gold.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Marry, and shall. But, how now, Sir John Hume!

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Seal up your lips, and give no words but mum;

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: The business asketh silent secrecy.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Dame Eleanor gives gold to bring the witch;

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Gold cannot come amiss, were she a devil.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Yet have I gold flies from another coast.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: I dare not say, from the rich cardinal

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: And from the great and new-made Duke of Suffolk,

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Yet I do find it so. For, to be plain,

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: They, knowing Dame Eleanor’s aspiring humour,

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Have hired me to undermine the Duchess

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: And buzz these conjurations in her brain.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: They say “A crafty knave does need no broker”,

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Yet am I Suffolk and the cardinal’s broker.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Hume, if you take not heed, you shall go near

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: To call them both a pair of crafty knaves.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Well, so its stands; and thus, I fear, at last

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Hume’s knavery will be the Duchess’ wrack,

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: And her attainture will be Humphrey’s fall.

lines.speaker: HUME
lines.text: Sort how it will, I shall have gold for all.
[_Exit._]
Enter Peter and Petitioners.
1 PETITIONER. My masters, let’s stand close. My Lord Protector will come this way by and by, and then we may deliver our supplications in the quill.
2 PETITIONER. Marry, the Lord protect him, for he’s a good man! Jesu bless him!
Enter Suffolk and Queen.
1 PETITIONER. Here he comes, methinks, and the Queen with him. I’ll be the first, sure.
2 PETITIONER. Come back, fool! This is the Duke of Suffolk and not my Lord Protector.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: How now, fellow; wouldst anything with me?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: 1 PETITIONER.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I pray, my lord, pardon me, I took ye for my Lord Protector.
[_Reading_.]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: “To my Lord Protector.” Are your supplications to his

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: lordship? Let me see them. What is thine?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: 1 PETITIONER.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Mine is, an ’t please your grace, against John Goodman, my Lord

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Cardinal’s man, for keeping my house and lands, and wife and all, from

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: me.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thy wife too! That’s some wrong, indeed.—What’s yours?—What’s here!
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: _Against the Duke of Suffolk for enclosing the commons of

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Melford._ How now, sir knave!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: 2 PETITIONER.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Alas, sir, I am but a poor petitioner of our whole township.
[_Giving his petition_.]

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Against my master, Thomas Horner, for saying

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: that the Duke of York was rightful heir to the crown.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What sayst thou? Did the Duke of York say he was rightful heir to the

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: crown?

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: That my master was? No, forsooth, my master said that he was, and that

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: the King was an usurper.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Who is there?
Enter Servant.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Take this fellow in, and send for his master with a pursuivant

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: presently.—We’ll hear more of your matter before the King.
[_Exit Servant with Peter._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And as for you, that love to be protected

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Under the wings of our Protector’s grace,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Begin your suits anew, and sue to him.
[_Tears the supplications._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Away, base cullions!—Suffolk, let them go.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Come, let’s be gone.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: My Lord of Suffolk, say, is this the guise,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Is this the fashion in the court of England?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Is this the government of Britain’s isle,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And this the royalty of Albion’s king?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What, shall King Henry be a pupil still

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Under the surly Gloucester’s governance?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Am I a queen in title and in style,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And must be made a subject to a duke?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I tell thee, Pole, when in the city Tours

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou ran’st atilt in honour of my love

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And stol’st away the ladies’ hearts of France,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I thought King Henry had resembled thee

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: In courage, courtship, and proportion.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But all his mind is bent to holiness,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To number Ave-Maries on his beads.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His champions are the prophets and apostles,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His weapons holy saws of sacred writ,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His study is his tilt-yard, and his loves

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Are brazen images of canonized saints.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I would the college of the cardinals

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Would choose him pope and carry him to Rome

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And set the triple crown upon his head!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That were a state fit for his holiness.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Madam, be patient. As I was cause

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Your highness came to England, so will I

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: In England work your grace’s full content.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Beside the haughty Protector, have we Beaufort

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The imperious churchman, Somerset, Buckingham,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And grumbling York; and not the least of these

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But can do more in England than the King.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And he of these that can do most of all

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Cannot do more in England than the Nevilles;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Salisbury and Warwick are no simple peers.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Not all these lords do vex me half so much

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As that proud dame, the Lord Protector’s wife.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: She sweeps it through the court with troops of ladies,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: More like an empress than Duke Humphrey’s wife.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Strangers in court do take her for the Queen.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: She bears a duke’s revenues on her back,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And in her heart she scorns our poverty.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Shall I not live to be avenged on her?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Contemptuous base-born callet as she is,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: She vaunted ’mongst her minions t’ other day

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The very train of her worst wearing gown

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Was better worth than all my father’s lands

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Till Suffolk gave two dukedoms for his daughter.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Madam, myself have limed a bush for her

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And placed a quire of such enticing birds

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That she will light to listen to the lays

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And never mount to trouble you again.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So let her rest; and, madam, list to me,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: For I am bold to counsel you in this:

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Although we fancy not the Cardinal,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Yet must we join with him and with the lords

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Till we have brought Duke Humphrey in disgrace.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As for the Duke of York, this late complaint

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Will make but little for his benefit.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So, one by one, we’ll weed them all at last,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And you yourself shall steer the happy helm.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Sound a sennet. Enter the King, Gloucester, Cardinal Beaufort,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Somerset, Buckingham, Salisbury, York, Warwick and the Duchess of

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Gloucester.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For my part, noble lords, I care not which;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or Somerset or York, all’s one to me.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: If York have ill demeaned himself in France,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then let him be denied the regentship.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: If Somerset be unworthy of the place,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Let York be regent; I will yield to him.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Whether your Grace be worthy, yea or no,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Dispute not that; York is the worthier.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Ambitious Warwick, let thy betters speak.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The Cardinal’s not my better in the field.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: All in this presence are thy betters, Warwick.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Warwick may live to be the best of all.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Peace, son!—And show some reason, Buckingham,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Why Somerset should be preferred in this.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Because the King, forsooth, will have it so.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Madam, the King is old enough himself

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To give his censure. These are no women’s matters.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If he be old enough, what needs your grace

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To be Protector of his excellence?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Madam, I am Protector of the realm,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And at his pleasure will resign my place.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Resign it then, and leave thine insolence.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Since thou wert king—as who is king but thou?—

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The commonwealth hath daily run to wrack,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The Dauphin hath prevailed beyond the seas,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And all the peers and nobles of the realm

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Have been as bondmen to thy sovereignty.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: The commons hast thou racked; the clergy’s bags

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Are lank and lean with thy extortions.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Thy sumptuous buildings and thy wife’s attire

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Have cost a mass of public treasury.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Thy cruelty in execution

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Upon offenders hath exceeded law,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And left thee to the mercy of the law.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thy sale of offices and towns in France,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If they were known, as the suspect is great,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Would make thee quickly hop without thy head.
[_Exit Gloucester. The Queen drops her fan._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Give me my fan. What minion! Can ye not?
[_She gives the Duchess a box on the ear._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I cry your mercy, madam; was it you?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Was’t I! Yea, I it was, proud Frenchwoman.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Could I come near your beauty with my nails,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: I’d set my ten commandments in your face.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sweet aunt, be quiet; ’twas against her will.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Against her will! Good King, look to ’t in time;

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: She’ll hamper thee and dandle thee like a baby.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Though in this place most master wear no breeches,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: She shall not strike Dame Eleanor unrevenged.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Lord Cardinal, I will follow Eleanor,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And listen after Humphrey, how he proceeds.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: She’s tickled now; her fume needs no spurs,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: She’ll gallop far enough to her destruction.
[_Exit._]
Enter Gloucester.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Now, lords, my choler being overblown

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: With walking once about the quadrangle,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I come to talk of commonwealth affairs.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As for your spiteful false objections,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Prove them, and I lie open to the law;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But God in mercy so deal with my soul

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As I in duty love my king and country!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But, to the matter that we have in hand:

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I say, my sovereign, York is meetest man

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To be your regent in the realm of France.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Before we make election, give me leave

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To show some reason, of no little force,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That York is most unmeet of any man.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I’ll tell thee, Suffolk, why I am unmeet:

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: First, for I cannot flatter thee in pride;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Next, if I be appointed for the place,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My Lord of Somerset will keep me here

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Without discharge, money, or furniture,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Till France be won into the Dauphin’s hands.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Last time, I danced attendance on his will

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Till Paris was besieged, famished, and lost.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That can I witness, and a fouler fact

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Did never traitor in the land commit.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Peace, headstrong Warwick!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Image of pride, why should I hold my peace?
Enter Horner the armourer and his man Peter, guarded.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Because here is a man accused of treason.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Pray God the Duke of York excuse himself!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Doth anyone accuse York for a traitor?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What mean’st thou, Suffolk? Tell me, what are these?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Please it your majesty, this is the man

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That doth accuse his master of high treason.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: His words were these: that Richard, Duke of York

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Was rightful heir unto the English crown,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And that your majesty was an usurper.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Say, man, were these thy words?

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: An ’t shall please your majesty, I never said nor thought any such

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: matter. God is my witness, I am falsely accused by the villain.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: By these ten bones, my lords, he did speak them to me in the garret one

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: night as we were scouring my Lord of York’s armour.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Base dunghill villain and mechanical,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I’ll have thy head for this thy traitor’s speech!—

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I do beseech your royal majesty,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Let him have all the rigour of the law.

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: Alas, my lord, hang me if ever I spake the words. My accuser is my

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: prentice; and when I did correct him for his fault the other day, he

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: did vow upon his knees he would be even with me. I have good witness of

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: this, therefore I beseech your majesty, do not cast away an honest man

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: for a villain’s accusation.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Uncle, what shall we say to this in law?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: This doom, my lord, if I may judge:

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Let Somerset be regent o’er the French,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Because in York this breeds suspicion;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And let these have a day appointed them

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: For single combat in convenient place,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: For he hath witness of his servant’s malice.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: This is the law, and this Duke Humphrey’s doom.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: I humbly thank your royal Majesty.

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: And I accept the combat willingly.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Alas, my lord, I cannot fight; for God’s sake, pity my case! The spite

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: of man prevaileth against me. O Lord, have mercy upon me! I shall never

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: be able to fight a blow. O Lord, my heart!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Sirrah, or you must fight or else be hanged.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Away with them to prison; and the day

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of combat shall be the last of the next month.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come, Somerset, we’ll see thee sent away.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]

lines.text: hear our exorcisms?

lines.text: I have heard her reported to be a woman of an invincible spirit. But it

lines.text: shall be convenient, Master Hume, that you be by her aloft while we be

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: busy below; and so, I pray you go, in God’s name, and leave us.
[_Exit Hume._]

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Well said, my masters; and welcome all. To this gear, the sooner the

lines.text: better.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE

lines.text: _First of the King: what shall of him become?_

[_Reads_.]

lines.text: _What shall befall the Duke of Somerset?_

lines.speaker: SPIRIT

lines.speaker: SPIRIT
lines.text: Safer shall he be upon the sandy plains

lines.speaker: SPIRIT
lines.text: Than where castles mounted stand.

lines.speaker: SPIRIT
lines.text: Have done, for more I hardly can endure.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Descend to darkness and the burning lake!

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: False fiend, avoid!

lines.text: Lay hands upon these traitors and their trash.

lines.text: Beldam, I think we watched you at an inch.

lines.text: Are deeply indebted for this piece of pains.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My Lord Protector will, I doubt it not,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: See you well guerdoned for these good deserts.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Not half so bad as thine to England’s king,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Injurious duke, that threatest where’s no cause.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: True, madam, none at all. What call you this?

lines.text: Away with them! Let them be clapped up close

lines.text: And kept asunder.—You, madam, shall with us.—

[_Exeunt above, Duchess and Hume, guarded._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: We’ll see your trinkets here all forthcoming.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: All, away!
[_Exeunt guard with  Jourdain, Southwell, Bolingbroke, etc._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Lord Buckingham, methinks you watched her well.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: A pretty plot, well chosen to build upon!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now, pray, my lord, let’s see the devil’s writ.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: What have we here?

lines.text: _The duke yet lives that Henry shall depose.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But him outlive and die a violent death._

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Why, this is just

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: _Aio te, Aeacida, Romanos vincere posse._

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Well, to the rest:

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: _Tell me what fate awaits the Duke of Suffolk?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: By water shall he die and take his end.

lines.text: What shall betide the Duke of Somerset?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Let him shun castles;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Safer shall he be upon the sandy plains

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Than where castles mounted stand._

lines.text: Come, come, my lords, these oracles

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Are hardly attained, and hardly understood.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The King is now in progress towards Saint Albans,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: With him the husband of this lovely lady.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Thither go these news as fast as horse can carry them.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: A sorry breakfast for my Lord Protector.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your Grace shall give me leave, my Lord of York,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To be the post, in hope of his reward.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: At your pleasure, my good lord.

lines.text: Who’s within there, ho!

lines.text: Invite my Lords of Salisbury and Warwick

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To sup with me tomorrow night. Away!

Enter the King, Queen, Gloucester, Cardinal and Suffolk with Falconers hallooing.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Believe me, lords, for flying at the brook

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I saw not better sport these seven years’ day;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yet, by your leave, the wind was very high,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And, ten to one, old Joan had not gone out.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But what a point, my lord, your falcon made,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And what a pitch she flew above the rest!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To see how God in all His creatures works!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yea, man and birds are fain of climbing high.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: No marvel, an it like your majesty,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: My Lord Protector’s hawks do tower so well;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: They know their master loves to be aloft,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And bears his thoughts above his falcon’s pitch.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: My lord, ’tis but a base ignoble mind

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That mounts no higher than a bird can soar.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: I thought as much. He would be above the clouds.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Ay, my Lord Cardinal, how think you by that?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Were it not good your grace could fly to heaven?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The treasury of everlasting joy.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Thy heaven is on earth; thine eyes and thoughts

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Beat on a crown, the treasure of thy heart,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Pernicious Protector, dangerous peer,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: That smooth’st it so with king and commonweal!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What, cardinal, is your priesthood grown peremptory?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: _Tantaene animis coelestibus irae?_

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Churchmen so hot? Good uncle, hide such malice.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: With such holiness can you do it?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: No malice, sir; no more than well becomes

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So good a quarrel and so bad a peer.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As who, my lord?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Why, as you, my lord,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: An ’t like your lordly Lord Protectorship.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Why, Suffolk, England knows thine insolence.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And thy ambition, Gloucester.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I prithee, peace, good queen,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And whet not on these furious peers;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For blessed are the peacemakers on earth.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Let me be blessed for the peace I make

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Against this proud Protector, with my sword!
[_Aside to Cardinal_.]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Faith, holy uncle, would ’twere come to that!
[_Aside to Gloucester_.]

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Marry, when thou dar’st.
[_Aside to Cardinal_.]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Make up no factious numbers for the matter,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: In thine own person answer thy abuse.
[_Aside to Gloucester_.]

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Ay, where thou dar’st not peep; an if thou

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: dar’st,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: This evening, on the east side of the grove.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How now, my lords?

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Believe me, cousin Gloucester,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Had not your man put up the fowl so suddenly,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: We had had more sport.—[_Aside to Gloucester_.]

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Come with thy two-hand sword.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: True, uncle.
[_Aside to Cardinal_.]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Are ye advised? The east side of the grove?
[_Aside to Gloucester_.]

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: I am with you.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, how now, uncle Gloucester?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Talking of hawking; nothing else, my lord.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Now, by God’s mother, priest,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I’ll shave your crown for this,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: _Medice, teipsum._—

lines.text: Protector, see to ’t well, protect yourself.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The winds grow high; so do your stomachs, lords.

lines.text: How irksome is this music to my heart!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When such strings jar, what hope of harmony?

lines.text: I pray, my lords, let me compound this strife.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What means this noise?

lines.text: Fellow, what miracle dost thou proclaim?

lines.text: A miracle! A miracle!

lines.text: Come to the King, and tell him what miracle.

lines.text: Forsooth, a blind man at Saint Alban’s shrine,

lines.text: Within this half hour, hath received his sight,

lines.text: A man that ne’er saw in his life before.

lines.text: Now, God be praised, that to believing souls

lines.text: Here comes the townsmen on procession,

lines.text: To present your highness with the man.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Great is his comfort in this earthly vale,

lines.text: Although by his sight his sin be multiplied.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Stand by, my masters. Bring him near the King.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: His highness’ pleasure is to talk with him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Good fellow, tell us here the circumstance,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That we for thee may glorify the Lord.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What, hast thou been long blind and now restored?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: Born blind, an ’t please your grace.

lines.speaker: WIFE
lines.text: Ay, indeed, was he.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: What woman is this?

lines.speaker: WIFE
lines.text: His wife, an ’t like your worship.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Hadst thou been his mother, thou couldst have better told.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Where wert thou born?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: At Berwick in the north, an ’t like your grace.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Poor soul, God’s goodness hath been great to thee.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let never day nor night unhallowed pass,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But still remember what the Lord hath done.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Tell me, good fellow, cam’st thou here by chance,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Or of devotion, to this holy shrine?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: God knows, of pure devotion; being called

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: A hundred times and oftener, in my sleep,

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: By good Saint Alban, who said “Simpcox, come,

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: Come, offer at my shrine, and I will help thee.”

lines.speaker: WIFE
lines.text: Most true, forsooth; and many time and oft

lines.speaker: WIFE
lines.text: Myself have heard a voice to call him so.

lines.text: What, art thou lame?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: Ay, God Almighty help me!

lines.text: How cam’st thou so?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: A fall off of a tree.

lines.text: A plum-tree, master.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: How long hast thou been blind?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: O, born so, master.

lines.text: What, and wouldst climb a tree?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: But that in all my life, when I was a youth.

lines.text: Too true; and bought his climbing very dear.

lines.text: Mass, thou lov’dst plums well, that wouldst venture so.

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: Alas, good master, my wife desired some damsons,

lines.text: And made me climb, with danger of my life.

lines.text: A subtle knave! But yet it shall not serve.—

lines.text: Let me see thine eyes. Wink now. Now open them.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: In my opinion yet thou seest not well.

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Sayst thou me so? What colour is this cloak of?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: Red, master, red as blood.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Why, that’s well said. What colour is my gown of?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: Black, forsooth, coal-black as jet.

lines.text: Why, then, thou know’st what colour jet is of?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And yet, I think, jet did he never see.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But cloaks and gowns before this day, a many.

lines.speaker: WIFE
lines.text: Never before this day in all his life.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Tell me, sirrah, what’s my name?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: Alas, master, I know not.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What’s his name?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: I know not.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Nor his?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: No, indeed, master.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What’s thine own name?

lines.text: Then, Sander, sit there, the lyingest knave in Christendom. If thou

lines.text: hadst been born blind, thou mightst as well have known all our names as

lines.text: colours; but suddenly to nominate them all, it is impossible.—My lords,

lines.text: Saint Alban here hath done a miracle; and would ye not think his

lines.text: cunning to be great that could restore this cripple to his legs again?

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: O master, that you could!

lines.text: My masters of Saint Albans, have you not beadles in your town, and

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: things called whips?

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Yes, my lord, if it please your grace.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Then send for one presently.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Sirrah, go fetch the beadle hither straight.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Now fetch me a stool hither by and by.—Now, sirrah, if you mean to save

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: yourself from whipping, leap me over this stool and run away.

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: Alas, master, I am not able to stand alone.

lines.speaker: SIMPCOX
lines.text: You go about to torture me in vain.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Well, sir, we must have you find your legs.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Sirrah beadle, whip him till he leap over that same stool.

lines.text: I will, my lord.—Come on, sirrah; off with your doublet quickly.

lines.text: Alas, master, what shall I do? I am not able to stand.

lines.text: O God, seest Thou this, and bearest so long?

lines.text: It made me laugh to see the villain run.

lines.text: Follow the knave, and take this drab away.

lines.text: Alas, sir, we did it for pure need.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Let them be whipped through every market town

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Till they come to Berwick, from whence they came.
[_Exeunt Wife, Beadle, Mayor, etc._]

lines.text: Duke Humphrey has done a miracle today.

lines.text: True, made the lame to leap and fly away.

lines.text: But you have done more miracles than I.

lines.text: You made in a day, my lord, whole towns to fly.

lines.text: What tidings with our cousin Buckingham?

lines.text: Such as my heart doth tremble to unfold.

lines.text: A sort of naughty persons, lewdly bent,

lines.text: Under the countenance and confederacy

lines.text: Of Lady Eleanor, the Protector’s wife,

lines.text: The ringleader and head of all this rout,

lines.text: Have practised dangerously against your state,

lines.text: Dealing with witches and with conjurers,

lines.text: Whom we have apprehended in the fact,

lines.text: Demanding of King Henry’s life and death,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: And so, my Lord Protector, by this means

lines.text: This news, I think, hath turned your weapon’s edge;

lines.text: ’Tis like, my lord, you will not keep your hour.

lines.text: Ambitious churchman, leave to afflict my heart.

lines.text: Sorrow and grief have vanquished all my powers,

lines.text: And, vanquished as I am, I yield to thee,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O God, what mischiefs work the wicked ones,

lines.text: Heaping confusion on their own heads thereby!

lines.text: Gloucester, see here the tainture of thy nest,

lines.text: And look thyself be faultless, thou wert best.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Madam, for myself, to heaven I do appeal

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: How I have loved my king and commonweal;

lines.text: And, for my wife, I know not how it stands.

lines.text: Sorry I am to hear what I have heard.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Noble she is; but if she have forgot

lines.text: Honour and virtue, and conversed with such

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As like to pitch defile nobility,

lines.text: I banish her my bed and company

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And give her as a prey to law and shame

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That hath dishonoured Gloucester’s honest name.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Well, for this night we will repose us here;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tomorrow toward London back again,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To look into this business thoroughly,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And call these foul offenders to their answers,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And poise the cause in Justice’ equal scales,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose beam stands sure, whose rightful cause prevails.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]

lines.text: Enter York, Salisbury and Warwick.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now, my good Lords of Salisbury and Warwick,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Our simple supper ended, give me leave

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In this close walk to satisfy myself

lines.text: In craving your opinion of my title,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Which is infallible, to England’s crown.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: My lord, I long to hear it at full.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Sweet York, begin; and if thy claim be good,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The Nevilles are thy subjects to command.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then thus:

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Edward the Third, my lords, had seven sons:

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The first, Edward the Black Prince, Prince of Wales;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The second, William of Hatfield; and the third,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Lionel, Duke of Clarence; next to whom

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The fifth was Edmund Langley, Duke of York;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The sixth was Thomas of Woodstock, Duke of Gloucester;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: William of Windsor was the seventh and last.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Edward the Black Prince died before his father

lines.text: And left behind him Richard, his only son,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Who after Edward the Third’s death reigned as king,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Till Henry Bolingbroke, Duke of Lancaster,

lines.text: The eldest son and heir of John of Gaunt,

lines.text: Crowned by the name of Henry the Fourth,

lines.text: Seized on the realm, deposed the rightful king,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Sent his poor queen to France, from whence she came,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And him to Pomfret; where, as all you know,

lines.text: Harmless Richard was murdered traitorously.

lines.text: Father, the Duke hath told the truth;
