lines.text: Thus got the house of Lancaster the crown.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Which now they hold by force and not by right;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For Richard, the first son’s heir, being dead,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The issue of the next son should have reigned.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: But William of Hatfield died without an heir.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The third son, Duke of Clarence, from whose line

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I claim the crown, had issue, Philippa, a daughter,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Who married Edmund Mortimer, Earl of March.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Edmund had issue, Roger, Earl of March;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Roger had issue, Edmund, Anne, and Eleanor.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: This Edmund, in the reign of Bolingbroke,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: As I have read, laid claim unto the crown

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And, but for Owen Glendower, had been king,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Who kept him in captivity till he died.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: But to the rest.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: His eldest sister, Anne,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My mother, being heir unto the crown,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Married Richard Earl of Cambridge, who was son

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To Edmund Langley, Edward the Third’s fifth son.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: By her I claim the kingdom; she was heir

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To Roger, Earl of March, who was the son

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Of Edmund Mortimer, who married Philippa,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Sole daughter unto Lionel, Duke of Clarence.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So, if the issue of the elder son

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Succeed before the younger, I am king.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: What plain proceeding is more plain than this?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Henry doth claim the crown from John of Gaunt,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The fourth son; York claims it from the third.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Till Lionel’s issue fails, his should not reign;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: It fails not yet, but flourishes in thee

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And in thy sons, fair slips of such a stock.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then, father Salisbury, kneel we together,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And in this private plot be we the first

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That shall salute our rightful sovereign

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With honour of his birthright to the crown.

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: Long live our sovereign Richard, England’s king!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: We thank you, lords. But I am not your king

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Till I be crowned, and that my sword be stained

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: With heart-blood of the house of Lancaster;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And that’s not suddenly to be performed,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But with advice and silent secrecy.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Do you as I do in these dangerous days—

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Wink at the Duke of Suffolk’s insolence,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: At Beaufort’s pride, at Somerset’s ambition,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: At Buckingham, and all the crew of them,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Till they have snared the shepherd of the flock,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That virtuous prince, the good Duke Humphrey.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: ’Tis that they seek; and they, in seeking that,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Shall find their deaths, if York can prophesy.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: My lord, break we off; we know your mind at full.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My heart assures me that the Earl of Warwick

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Shall one day make the Duke of York a king.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And, Neville, this I do assure myself:

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Richard shall live to make the Earl of Warwick

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The greatest man in England but the king.
[_Exeunt._]
Sound trumpets. Enter the King, the Queen, Gloucester, York, Suffolk and Salisbury; the Duchess of Gloucester, Margery Jourdain, Southwell, Hume and Bolingbroke under guard.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Stand forth, Dame Eleanor Cobham, Gloucester’s wife.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: In sight of God and us, your guilt is great;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Receive the sentence of the law for sins

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Such as by God’s book are adjudged to death.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: You four, from hence to prison back again;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: From thence unto the place of execution.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The witch in Smithfield shall be burnt to ashes,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And you three shall be strangled on the gallows.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: You, madam, for you are more nobly born,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Despoiled of your honour in your life,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall, after three days’ open penance done,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Live in your country here in banishment,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With Sir John Stanley in the Isle of Man.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Welcome is banishment; welcome were my death.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Eleanor, the law, thou seest, hath judged thee.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I cannot justify whom the law condemns.
[_Exeunt Duchess and the other prisoners, guarded._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Mine eyes are full of tears, my heart of grief.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Ah, Humphrey, this dishonour in thine age

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Will bring thy head with sorrow to the ground!—

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I beseech your majesty, give me leave to go;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Sorrow would solace, and mine age would ease.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Stay, Humphrey Duke of Gloucester. Ere thou go,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Give up thy staff. Henry will to himself

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Protector be; and God shall be my hope,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My stay, my guide, and lantern to my feet.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And go in peace, Humphrey, no less beloved

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than when thou wert Protector to thy king.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I see no reason why a king of years

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Should be to be protected like a child.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: God and King Henry govern England’s realm!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Give up your staff, sir, and the King his realm.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: My staff? Here, noble Henry, is my staff.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As willingly do I the same resign

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As e’er thy father Henry made it mine;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And even as willingly at thy feet I leave it

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As others would ambitiously receive it.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Farewell, good King. When I am dead and gone,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: May honourable peace attend thy throne.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why, now is Henry King and Margaret Queen,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And Humphrey Duke of Gloucester scarce himself,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That bears so shrewd a maim. Two pulls at once;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His lady banished, and a limb lopped off.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: This staff of honour raught, there let it stand

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Where it best fits to be, in Henry’s hand.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thus droops this lofty pine and hangs his sprays;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thus Eleanor’s pride dies in her youngest days.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Lords, let him go.—Please it your majesty,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: This is the day appointed for the combat,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And ready are the appellant and defendant,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The armourer and his man, to enter the lists,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So please your highness to behold the fight.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ay, good my lord; for purposely therefore

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Left I the court to see this quarrel tried.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I’ God’s name, see the lists and all things fit.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here let them end it, and God defend the right!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I never saw a fellow worse bested,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Or more afraid to fight, than is the appellant,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The servant of his armourer, my lords.

Enter at one door Horner the armourer, and his Neighbours, drinking to him so much that he is drunk; and he enters with a drum before him and his staff with a sandbag fastened to it; and at the other door Peter, his man, with a drum and sandbag, and Prentices  drinking to him.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: 1 NEIGHBOUR.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Here, neighbour Horner, I drink to you in a cup of sack; and fear not,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: neighbour, you shall do well enough.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: 2 NEIGHBOUR.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And here, neighbour, here’s a cup of charneco.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: 3 NEIGHBOUR.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And here’s a pot of good double beer, neighbour. Drink, and fear not

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: your man.

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: Let it come, i’ faith, and I’ll pledge you all; and a fig for Peter!

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: 1 PRENTICE.

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: Here, Peter, I drink to thee, and be not afraid.

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: 2 PRENTICE.

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: Be merry, Peter, and fear not thy master. Fight for credit of the

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: prentices.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: I thank you all. Drink, and pray for me, I pray you, for I think I have

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: taken my last draught in this world. Here, Robin, an if I die, I give

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: thee my apron; and, Will, thou shalt have my hammer; and here, Tom,

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: take all the money that I have. O Lord bless me! I pray God, for I am

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: never able to deal with my master, he hath learnt so much fence

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: already.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Come, leave your drinking and fall to blows.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Sirrah, what’s thy name?

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Peter, forsooth.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Peter? What more?

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Thump.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Thump! Then see thou thump thy master well.

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: Masters, I am come hither, as it were, upon my man’s instigation, to

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: prove him a knave and myself an honest man; and touching the Duke of

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: York, I will take my death I never meant him any ill, nor the King, nor

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: the Queen; and therefore, Peter, have at thee with a downright blow!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Dispatch! This knave’s tongue begins to double.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Sound, trumpets. Alarum to the combatants!
[_They fight, and Peter strikes him down._]

lines.speaker: HORNER
lines.text: Hold, Peter, hold! I confess, I confess treason.
[_Dies._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Take away his weapon.—Fellow, thank God and the good wine in thy

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: master’s way.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: O God, have I overcome mine enemies in this presence? O Peter, thou

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: hast prevailed in right!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go, take hence that traitor from our sight,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For by his death we do perceive his guilt.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And God in justice hath revealed to us

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The truth and innocence of this poor fellow,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Which he had thought to have murdered wrongfully.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come, fellow, follow us for thy reward.
[_Sound a flourish. Exeunt._]
Enter Gloucester and his Servingmen in mourning cloaks.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thus sometimes hath the brightest day a cloud,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And after summer evermore succeeds

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Barren winter, with his wrathful nipping cold;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: So cares and joys abound, as seasons fleet.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Sirs, what’s o’clock?

lines.speaker: SERVINGMEN
lines.text: Ten, my lord.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Ten is the hour that was appointed me

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To watch the coming of my punished duchess.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Uneath may she endure the flinty streets,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To tread them with her tender-feeling feet.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Sweet Nell, ill can thy noble mind abrook

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The abject people gazing on thy face

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: With envious looks, laughing at thy shame,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That erst did follow thy proud chariot wheels

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: When thou didst ride in triumph through the streets.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But, soft! I think she comes; and I’ll prepare

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: My tear-stained eyes to see her miseries.
Enter the Duchess of Gloucester in a white sheet, and a taper burning in her hand; with Sir John Stanley, the Sheriff, and Officers.

lines.speaker: SERVINGMEN
lines.text: So please your Grace, we’ll take her from the sheriff.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: No, stir not for your lives; let her pass by.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Come you, my lord, to see my open shame?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Now thou dost penance too. Look how they gaze!

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: See how the giddy multitude do point,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And nod their heads, and throw their eyes on thee.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Ah, Gloucester, hide thee from their hateful looks,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And, in thy closet pent up, rue my shame,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And ban thine enemies, both mine and thine!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Be patient, gentle Nell, forget this grief.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Ah, Gloucester, teach me to forget myself!

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: For whilst I think I am thy married wife

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And thou a prince, Protector of this land,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Methinks I should not thus be led along,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Mailed up in shame, with papers on my back,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And followed with a rabble that rejoice

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: To see my tears and hear my deep-fet groans.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: The ruthless flint doth cut my tender feet,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And when I start, the envious people laugh

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And bid me be advised how I tread.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Ah, Humphrey, can I bear this shameful yoke?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Trowest thou that e’er I’ll look upon the world,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Or count them happy that enjoy the sun?

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: No, dark shall be my light and night my day;

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: To think upon my pomp shall be my hell.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Sometimes I’ll say, I am Duke Humphrey’s wife,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And he a prince and ruler of the land;

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Yet so he ruled and such a prince he was

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: As he stood by whilst I, his forlorn duchess,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Was made a wonder and a pointing-stock

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: To every idle rascal follower.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: But be thou mild and blush not at my shame,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Nor stir at nothing till the axe of death

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Hang over thee, as, sure, it shortly will.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: For Suffolk, he that can do all in all

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: With her that hateth thee and hates us all,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And York and impious Beaufort, that false priest,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Have all limed bushes to betray thy wings;

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And fly thou how thou canst, they’ll tangle thee.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: But fear not thou until thy foot be snared,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Nor never seek prevention of thy foes.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Ah, Nell, forbear! Thou aimest all awry.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I must offend before I be attainted;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And had I twenty times so many foes,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And each of them had twenty times their power,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: All these could not procure me any scathe

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: So long as I am loyal, true, and crimeless.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Wouldst have me rescue thee from this reproach?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Why, yet thy scandal were not wiped away,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But I in danger for the breach of law.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thy greatest help is quiet, gentle Nell.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I pray thee, sort thy heart to patience;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: These few days’ wonder will be quickly worn.
Enter a Herald.

lines.speaker: HERALD
lines.text: I summon your grace to his majesty’s parliament,

lines.speaker: HERALD
lines.text: Holden at Bury the first of this next month.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And my consent ne’er asked herein before?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: This is close dealing. Well, I will be there.
[_Exit Herald._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: My Nell, I take my leave; and, master sheriff,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Let not her penance exceed the King’s commission.

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: An ’t please your grace, here my commission stays,

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: And Sir John Stanley is appointed now

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: To take her with him to the Isle of Man.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Must you, Sir John, protect my lady here?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: So am I given in charge, may ’t please your grace.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Entreat her not the worse in that I pray

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: You use her well. The world may laugh again,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And I may live to do you kindness if

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: You do it her. And so, Sir John, farewell.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: What, gone, my lord, and bid me not farewell?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Witness my tears, I cannot stay to speak.
[_Exeunt Gloucester and Servingmen._]

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Art thou gone too? All comfort go with thee,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: For none abides with me; my joy is death;

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Death, at whose name I oft have been afeard,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Because I wished this world’s eternity.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Stanley, I prithee, go, and take me hence,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: I care not whither, for I beg no favour,

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: Only convey me where thou art commanded.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Why, madam, that is to the Isle of Man,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: There to be used according to your state.

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: That’s bad enough, for I am but reproach;

lines.speaker: ELEANOR
lines.text: And shall I then be used reproachfully?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Like to a duchess, and Duke Humphrey’s lady;

lines.speaker: STANLEY

lines.text: And never asked for restitution.

lines.text: And yet, good Humphrey, is the hour to come

lines.text: That e’er I proved thee false or feared thy faith.

lines.text: Beguiles him, as the mournful crocodile

lines.text: I tender so the safety of my liege.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Here is my hand, the deed is worthy doing.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And so say I.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And I. And now we three have spoke it,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: It skills not greatly who impugns our doom.
Enter a Post.

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: Great lords, from Ireland am I come amain

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: To signify that rebels there are up

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: And put the Englishmen unto the sword.

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: Send succours, lords, and stop the rage betime,

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: Before the wound do grow uncurable;

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: For, being green, there is great hope of help.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: A breach that craves a quick expedient stop!

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: What counsel give you in this weighty cause?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That Somerset be sent as regent thither.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: ’Tis meet that lucky ruler be employed;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Witness the fortune he hath had in France.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: If York, with all his far-fet policy,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Had been the regent there instead of me,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: He never would have stayed in France so long.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: No, not to lose it all as thou hast done.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I rather would have lost my life betimes

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Than bring a burden of dishonour home

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: By staying there so long till all were lost.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Show me one scar charactered on thy skin;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Men’s flesh preserved so whole do seldom win.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Nay then, this spark will prove a raging fire

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If wind and fuel be brought to feed it with.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: No more, good York. Sweet Somerset, be still.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thy fortune, York, hadst thou been regent there,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Might happily have proved far worse than his.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: What, worse than naught? Nay, then a shame take all!

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And, in the number, thee that wishest shame!

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: My Lord of York, try what your fortune is.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Th’ uncivil kerns of Ireland are in arms

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: And temper clay with blood of Englishmen.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: To Ireland will you lead a band of men,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Collected choicely, from each county some,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: And try your hap against the Irishmen?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I will, my lord, so please his majesty.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Why, our authority is his consent,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And what we do establish he confirms.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Then, noble York, take thou this task in hand.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I am content. Provide me soldiers, lords,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whiles I take order for mine own affairs.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: A charge, Lord York, that I will see performed.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But now return we to the false Duke Humphrey.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: No more of him; for I will deal with him

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: That henceforth he shall trouble us no more.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: And so break off; the day is almost spent.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Lord Suffolk, you and I must talk of that event.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My Lord of Suffolk, within fourteen days

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: At Bristol I expect my soldiers;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For there I’ll ship them all for Ireland.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I’ll see it truly done, my Lord of York.
[_Exeunt all but York._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now, York, or never, steel thy fearful thoughts,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And change misdoubt to resolution.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Be that thou hop’st to be, or what thou art

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Resign to death; it is not worth th’ enjoying.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Let pale-faced fear keep with the mean-born man

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And find no harbour in a royal heart.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Faster than springtime showers comes thought on thought,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And not a thought but thinks on dignity.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My brain, more busy than the labouring spider

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Weaves tedious snares to trap mine enemies.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Well, nobles, well, ’tis politicly done,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To send me packing with an host of men;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I fear me you but warm the starved snake,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Who, cherished in your breasts, will sting your hearts.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: ’Twas men I lacked, and you will give them me;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I take it kindly, yet be well assured

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: You put sharp weapons in a madman’s hands.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whiles I in Ireland nourish a mighty band,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I will stir up in England some black storm

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Shall blow ten thousand souls to heaven or hell;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And this fell tempest shall not cease to rage

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Until the golden circuit on my head,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Like to the glorious sun’s transparent beams,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Do calm the fury of this mad-bred flaw.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And for a minister of my intent,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I have seduced a headstrong Kentishman,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: John Cade of Ashford,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To make commotion, as full well he can,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Under the title of John Mortimer.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In Ireland have I seen this stubborn Cade

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Oppose himself against a troop of kerns,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And fought so long till that his thighs with darts

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Were almost like a sharp-quilled porpentine;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And in the end being rescued, I have seen

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Him caper upright like a wild Morisco,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Shaking the bloody darts as he his bells.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Full often, like a shag-haired crafty kern,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Hath he conversed with the enemy,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And undiscovered come to me again

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And given me notice of their villainies.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: This devil here shall be my substitute;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For that John Mortimer, which now is dead,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In face, in gait, in speech, he doth resemble.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: By this I shall perceive the commons’ mind,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: How they affect the house and claim of York.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Say he be taken, racked, and tortured,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I know no pain they can inflict upon him

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Will make him say I moved him to those arms.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Say that he thrive, as ’tis great like he will,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Why then from Ireland come I with my strength

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And reap the harvest which that rascal sowed.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For Humphrey being dead, as he shall be,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And Henry put apart, the next for me.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Bury St. Edmund’s. A Room of State

lines.text: Enter two or three Murderers running over the stage, from the murder of Duke Humphrey.
1 MURDERER. Run to my Lord of Suffolk; let him know We have dispatched the Duke as he commanded.
2 MURDERER. O that it were to do! What have we done? Didst ever hear a man so penitent?
Enter Suffolk.
1 MURDERER. Here comes my lord.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Now, sirs, have you dispatched this thing?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: 1 MURDERER.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Ay, my good lord, he’s dead.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Why, that’s well said. Go, get you to my house;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I will reward you for this venturous deed.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The King and all the peers are here at hand.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Have you laid fair the bed? Is all things well,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: According as I gave directions?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: 1 MURDERER.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: ’Tis, my good lord.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Away, be gone!
[_Exeunt Murderers._]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Sound trumpets. Enter the King, the Queen, Cardinal Beaufort, Somerset

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: with attendants.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go, call our uncle to our presence straight;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Say we intend to try his grace today

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If he be guilty, as ’tis published.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I’ll call him presently, my noble lord.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lords, take your places; and, I pray you all,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Proceed no straiter ’gainst our uncle Gloucester

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than from true evidence of good esteem

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: He be approved in practice culpable.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: God forbid any malice should prevail

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That faultless may condemn a nobleman!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Pray God he may acquit him of suspicion!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I thank thee, Meg; these words content me much.
Enter Suffolk.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How now? Why look’st thou pale? Why tremblest thou?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Where is our uncle? What’s the matter, Suffolk?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Dead in his bed, my lord; Gloucester is dead.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Marry, God forfend!

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: God’s secret judgment! I did dream tonight

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: The Duke was dumb and could not speak a word.
[_The King swoons._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: How fares my lord? Help, lords! the King is dead.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Rear up his body; wring him by the nose.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Run, go, help, help! O Henry, ope thine eyes!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: He doth revive again. Madam, be patient.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O heavenly God!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: How fares my gracious lord?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Comfort, my sovereign! Gracious Henry, comfort!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What, doth my Lord of Suffolk comfort me?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Came he right now to sing a raven’s note,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose dismal tune bereft my vital powers,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And thinks he that the chirping of a wren,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: By crying comfort from a hollow breast,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Can chase away the first-conceived sound?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Hide not thy poison with such sugared words;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lay not thy hands on me. Forbear, I say!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Their touch affrights me as a serpent’s sting.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou baleful messenger, out of my sight!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Upon thy eyeballs murderous tyranny

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sits in grim majesty to fright the world.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Look not upon me, for thine eyes are wounding.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yet do not go away; come, basilisk,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And kill the innocent gazer with thy sight.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For in the shade of death I shall find joy,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: In life but double death, now Gloucester’s dead.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why do you rate my Lord of Suffolk thus?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Although the Duke was enemy to him,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yet he most Christian-like laments his death.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And for myself, foe as he was to me,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Might liquid tears or heart-offending groans

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Or blood-consuming sighs recall his life,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I would be blind with weeping, sick with groans,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Look pale as primrose with blood-drinking sighs,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And all to have the noble Duke alive.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What know I how the world may deem of me?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For it is known we were but hollow friends.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: It may be judged I made the Duke away;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: So shall my name with slander’s tongue be wounded

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And princes’ courts be filled with my reproach.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: This get I by his death. Ay me, unhappy!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To be a queen, and crowned with infamy!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ah, woe is me for Gloucester, wretched man!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Be woe for me, more wretched than he is.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What, dost thou turn away and hide thy face?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I am no loathsome leper. Look on me.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What, art thou, like the adder, waxen deaf?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Be poisonous too and kill thy forlorn Queen.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Is all thy comfort shut in Gloucester’s tomb?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why, then, Dame Margaret was ne’er thy joy.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Erect his statue and worship it,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And make my image but an alehouse sign.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Was I for this nigh wracked upon the sea

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And twice by awkward wind from England’s bank

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Drove back again unto my native clime?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What boded this, but well forewarning wind

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Did seem to say “Seek not a scorpion’s nest,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Nor set no footing on this unkind shore?”

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What did I then, but cursed the gentle gusts

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And he that loosed them forth their brazen caves

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And bid them blow towards England’s blessed shore

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Or turn our stern upon a dreadful rock?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yet Aeolus would not be a murderer,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But left that hateful office unto thee.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The pretty-vaulting sea refused to drown me,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Knowing that thou wouldst have me drowned on shore

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: With tears as salt as sea, through thy unkindness.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The splitting rocks cowered in the sinking sands

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And would not dash me with their ragged sides,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Because thy flinty heart, more hard than they,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Might in thy palace perish Margaret.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As far as I could ken thy chalky cliffs,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: When from thy shore the tempest beat us back,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I stood upon the hatches in the storm,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And when the dusky sky began to rob

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: My earnest-gaping sight of thy land’s view,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I took a costly jewel from my neck—

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: A heart it was, bound in with diamonds—

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And threw it towards thy land. The sea received it,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And so I wished thy body might my heart.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And even with this I lost fair England’s view,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And bid mine eyes be packing with my heart,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And called them blind and dusky spectacles,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For losing ken of Albion’s wished coast.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: How often have I tempted Suffolk’s tongue,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The agent of thy foul inconstancy,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To sit and witch me, as Ascanius did

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: When he to madding Dido would unfold

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His father’s acts commenced in burning Troy!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Am I not witched like her? Or thou not false like him?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ay me, I can no more! Die, Margaret,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For Henry weeps that thou dost live so long.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Noise within. Enter Warwick, Salisbury and many Commons.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: It is reported, mighty sovereign,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That good Duke Humphrey traitorously is murdered

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: By Suffolk and the Cardinal Beaufort’s means.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The commons, like an angry hive of bees

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That want their leader, scatter up and down

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And care not who they sting in his revenge.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Myself have calmed their spleenful mutiny,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Until they hear the order of his death.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That he is dead, good Warwick, ’tis too true;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But how he died God knows, not Henry.
Enter his chamber, view his breathless corpse, And comment then upon his sudden death.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That shall I do, my liege.—Stay, Salisbury,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With the rude multitude till I return.
[_Warwick exits through one door; Salisbury and Commons exit through another._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O Thou that judgest all things, stay my thoughts,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My thoughts that labour to persuade my soul

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Some violent hands were laid on Humphrey’s life.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If my suspect be false, forgive me, God,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For judgment only doth belong to Thee.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Fain would I go to chafe his paly lips

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With twenty thousand kisses, and to drain

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Upon his face an ocean of salt tears,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To tell my love unto his dumb deaf trunk,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And with my fingers feel his hand unfeeling;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But all in vain are these mean obsequies.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And to survey his dead and earthy image,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What were it but to make my sorrow greater?
Enter Warwick and others, bearing Gloucester’s body on a bed.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Come hither, gracious sovereign, view this body.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That is to see how deep my grave is made,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For with his soul fled all my worldly solace;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For seeing him, I see my life in death.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: As surely as my soul intends to live

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With that dread King that took our state upon Him

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To free us from His Father’s wrathful curse,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I do believe that violent hands were laid

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Upon the life of this thrice-famed duke.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: A dreadful oath, sworn with a solemn tongue!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: What instance gives Lord Warwick for his vow?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: See how the blood is settled in his face.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Oft have I seen a timely-parted ghost,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Of ashy semblance, meagre, pale, and bloodless,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Being all descended to the labouring heart,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Who, in the conflict that it holds with death,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Attracts the same for aidance ’gainst the enemy,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Which with the heart there cools and ne’er returneth

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To blush and beautify the cheek again.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But see, his face is black and full of blood,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: His eyeballs further out than when he lived,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Staring full ghastly like a strangled man;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: His hair upreared, his nostrils stretched with struggling,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: His hands abroad displayed, as one that grasped

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And tugged for life and was by strength subdued.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Look, on the sheets his hair, you see, is sticking;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: His well-proportioned beard made rough and rugged,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Like to the summer’s corn by tempest lodged.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: It cannot be but he was murdered here;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The least of all these signs were probable.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Why, Warwick, who should do the Duke to death?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Myself and Beaufort had him in protection,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And we, I hope, sir, are no murderers.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But both of you were vowed Duke Humphrey’s foes,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And you, forsooth, had the good Duke to keep.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: ’Tis like you would not feast him like a friend,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And ’tis well seen he found an enemy.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Then you, belike, suspect these noblemen

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As guilty of Duke Humphrey’s timeless death.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Who finds the heifer dead and bleeding fresh

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And sees fast by a butcher with an axe,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But will suspect ’twas he that made the slaughter?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Who finds the partridge in the puttock’s nest

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But may imagine how the bird was dead,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Although the kite soar with unbloodied beak?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Even so suspicious is this tragedy.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Are you the butcher, Suffolk? Where’s your knife?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Is Beaufort termed a kite? Where are his talons?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I wear no knife to slaughter sleeping men,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But here’s a vengeful sword, rusted with ease,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That shall be scoured in his rancorous heart

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That slanders me with murder’s crimson badge.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Say, if thou dar’st, proud Lord of Warwickshire,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That I am faulty in Duke Humphrey’s death.
[_Exeunt Cardinal, Somerset and others._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: What dares not Warwick, if false Suffolk dare him?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: He dares not calm his contumelious spirit,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Nor cease to be an arrogant controller,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Though Suffolk dare him twenty thousand times.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Madam, be still, with reverence may I say;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For every word you speak in his behalf

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Is slander to your royal dignity.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Blunt-witted lord, ignoble in demeanour!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: If ever lady wronged her lord so much,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thy mother took into her blameful bed

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Some stern untutored churl, and noble stock

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Was graft with crab-tree slip, whose fruit thou art,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And never of the Nevilles’ noble race.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But that the guilt of murder bucklers thee

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And I should rob the deathsman of his fee,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Quitting thee thereby of ten thousand shames,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And that my sovereign’s presence makes me mild,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I would, false murderous coward, on thy knee

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Make thee beg pardon for thy passed speech

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And say it was thy mother that thou meant’st,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That thou thyself wast born in bastardy;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And after all this fearful homage done,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Give thee thy hire and send thy soul to hell,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Pernicious blood-sucker of sleeping men!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thou shalt be waking while I shed thy blood,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: If from this presence thou dar’st go with me.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Away even now, or I will drag thee hence.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Unworthy though thou art, I’ll cope with thee

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And do some service to Duke Humphrey’s ghost.
[_Exeunt Suffolk and Warwick._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What stronger breastplate than a heart untainted?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thrice is he armed that hath his quarrel just,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And he but naked, though locked up in steel,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose conscience with injustice is corrupted.
[_A noise within._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What noise is this?
Enter Suffolk and Warwick with their weapons drawn.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, how now, lords? Your wrathful weapons drawn

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here in our presence? Dare you be so bold?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, what tumultuous clamour have we here?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The traitorous Warwick with the men of Bury

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Set all upon me, mighty sovereign.
Enter Salisbury.
[_To the Commons, entering_.]

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Sirs, stand apart; the King shall know your mind.—

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Dread lord, the commons send you word by me,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Unless Lord Suffolk straight be done to death,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Or banished fair England’s territories,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: They will by violence tear him from your palace

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And torture him with grievous lingering death.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: They say, by him the good Duke Humphrey died;

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: They say, in him they fear your highness’ death;

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And mere instinct of love and loyalty,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Free from a stubborn opposite intent,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: As being thought to contradict your liking,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Makes them thus forward in his banishment.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: They say, in care of your most royal person,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: That if your highness should intend to sleep

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And charge that no man should disturb your rest,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: In pain of your dislike or pain of death,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Yet, notwithstanding such a strait edict,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Were there a serpent seen, with forked tongue,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: That slyly glided towards your majesty,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: It were but necessary you were waked,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Lest, being suffered in that harmful slumber,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: The mortal worm might make the sleep eternal.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And therefore do they cry, though you forbid,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: That they will guard you, whe’er you will or no,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: From such fell serpents as false Suffolk is,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: With whose envenomed and fatal sting

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Your loving uncle, twenty times his worth,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: They say, is shamefully bereft of life.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: COMMONS
lines.text: An answer from the King, my Lord of Salisbury!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: ’Tis like the commons, rude unpolished hinds,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Could send such message to their sovereign.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But you, my lord, were glad to be employed,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To show how quaint an orator you are.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But all the honour Salisbury hath won

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Is that he was the lord ambassador

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Sent from a sort of tinkers to the King.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: COMMONS
lines.text: An answer from the King, or we will all break in!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go, Salisbury, and tell them all from me,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I thank them for their tender loving care;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And had I not been cited so by them,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yet did I purpose as they do entreat.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For, sure, my thoughts do hourly prophesy

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Mischance unto my state by Suffolk’s means.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And therefore, by His majesty I swear,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose far unworthy deputy I am,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: He shall not breathe infection in this air

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But three days longer, on the pain of death.
[_Exit Salisbury._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O Henry, let me plead for gentle Suffolk!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ungentle Queen, to call him gentle Suffolk!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No more, I say; if thou dost plead for him,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou wilt but add increase unto my wrath.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Had I but said, I would have kept my word;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But when I swear, it is irrevocable.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If, after three days’ space, thou here be’st found

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: On any ground that I am ruler of,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The world shall not be ransom for thy life.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come, Warwick, come, good Warwick, go with me;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I have great matters to impart to thee.
[_Exeunt all but Queen and Suffolk._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Mischance and sorrow go along with you!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Heart’s discontent and sour affliction

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Be playfellows to keep you company!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: There’s two of you; the devil make a third!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And threefold vengeance tend upon your steps!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Cease, gentle Queen, these execrations,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And let thy Suffolk take his heavy leave.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Fie, coward woman and soft-hearted wretch!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Has thou not spirit to curse thine enemies?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: A plague upon them! Wherefore should I curse them?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Could curses kill, as doth the mandrake’s groan,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I would invent as bitter searching terms,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As curst, as harsh and horrible to hear,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Delivered strongly through my fixed teeth,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: With full as many signs of deadly hate,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As lean-faced Envy in her loathsome cave.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: My tongue should stumble in mine earnest words;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Mine eyes should sparkle like the beaten flint;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Mine hair be fixed on end, as one distract;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Ay, every joint should seem to curse and ban;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And even now my burdened heart would break

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Should I not curse them. Poison be their drink!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Gall, worse than gall, the daintiest that they taste!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Their sweetest shade a grove of cypress-trees!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Their chiefest prospect murdering basilisks;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Their softest touch as smart as lizards’ stings!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Their music frightful as the serpent’s hiss,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And boding screech-owls make the consort full!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: All the foul terrors in dark-seated hell—

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Enough, sweet Suffolk; thou torment’st thyself,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And these dread curses, like the sun ’gainst glass,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Or like an overcharged gun, recoil

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And turns the force of them upon thyself.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: You bade me ban, and will you bid me leave?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Now, by the ground that I am banished from,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Well could I curse away a winter’s night,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Though standing naked on a mountain top

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Where biting cold would never let grass grow,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And think it but a minute spent in sport.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, let me entreat thee cease. Give me thy hand,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That I may dew it with my mournful tears;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Nor let the rain of heaven wet this place

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To wash away my woeful monuments.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, could this kiss be printed in thy hand,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That thou mightst think upon these by the seal,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Through whom a thousand sighs are breathed for thee!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: So, get thee gone, that I may know my grief;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: ’Tis but surmised whiles thou art standing by,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As one that surfeits thinking on a want.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I will repeal thee, or, be well assured,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Adventure to be banished myself;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And banished I am, if but from thee.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Go; speak not to me, even now be gone!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, go not yet! Even thus two friends condemned

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Embrace and kiss and take ten thousand leaves,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Loather a hundred times to part than die.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yet now farewell, and farewell life with thee.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thus is poor Suffolk ten times banished,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Once by the King, and three times thrice by thee.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: ’Tis not the land I care for, wert thou thence.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: A wilderness is populous enough,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So Suffolk had thy heavenly company;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: For where thou art, there is the world itself,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: With every several pleasure in the world;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And where thou art not, desolation.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I can no more. Live thou to joy thy life,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Myself no joy in nought but that thou liv’st.
Enter Vaux.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Whither goes Vaux so fast? What news, I prithee?

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: To signify unto his majesty

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: That Cardinal Beaufort is at point of death;

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: For suddenly a grievous sickness took him,

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: That makes him gasp and stare and catch the air,

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: Blaspheming God and cursing men on earth.

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: Sometime he talks as if Duke Humphrey’s ghost

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: Were by his side; sometime he calls the King

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: And whispers to his pillow, as to him,

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: The secrets of his overcharged soul.

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: And I am sent to tell his majesty

lines.speaker: VAUX
lines.text: That even now he cries aloud for him.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Go tell this heavy message to the King.
[_Exit Vaux._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ay me! What is this world? What news are these!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But wherefore grieve I at an hour’s poor loss,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Omitting Suffolk’s exile, my soul’s treasure?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why only, Suffolk, mourn I not for thee,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And with the southern clouds contend in tears,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Theirs for the earth’s increase, mine for my sorrows’?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Now get thee hence. The King, thou know’st, is coming;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If thou be found by me thou art but dead.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: If I depart from thee, I cannot live;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And in thy sight to die, what were it else

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But like a pleasant slumber in thy lap?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Here could I breathe my soul into the air,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As mild and gentle as the cradle-babe

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Dying with mother’s dug between its lips;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Where, from thy sight, I should be raging mad

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And cry out for thee to close up mine eyes,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To have thee with thy lips to stop my mouth.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So shouldst thou either turn my flying soul,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Or I should breathe it so into thy body,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And then it lived in sweet Elysium.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To die by thee were but to die in jest;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: From thee to die were torture more than death.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: O, let me stay, befall what may befall!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Away! Though parting be a fretful corrosive,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: It is applied to a deathful wound.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To France, sweet Suffolk! Let me hear from thee,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For whereso’er thou art in this world’s globe

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I’ll have an Iris that shall find thee out.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I go.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And take my heart with thee.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: A jewel, locked into the woefull’st cask

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That ever did contain a thing of worth.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Even as a splitted bark, so sunder we.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: This way fall I to death.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: This way for me.
[_Exeunt severally._]
Enter the King, Salisbury and Warwick, to the Cardinal in bed.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How fares my lord? Speak, Beaufort, to thy sovereign.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: If thou be’st Death, I’ll give thee England’s treasure,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Enough to purchase such another island,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: So thou wilt let me live and feel no pain.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ah, what a sign it is of evil life

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Where death’s approach is seen so terrible!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Beaufort, it is thy sovereign speaks to thee.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Bring me unto my trial when you will.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Died he not in his bed? Where should he die?

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Can I make men live, whe’er they will or no?

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: O, torture me no more! I will confess.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Alive again? Then show me where he is.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: I’ll give a thousand pound to look upon him.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: He hath no eyes, the dust hath blinded them.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Comb down his hair; look, look, it stands upright,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Like lime-twigs set to catch my winged soul.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Give me some drink, and bid the apothecary

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Bring the strong poison that I bought of him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O Thou eternal mover of the heavens,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Look with a gentle eye upon this wretch!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O, beat away the busy meddling fiend

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That lays strong siege unto this wretch’s soul,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And from his bosom purge this black despair!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: See how the pangs of death do make him grin!

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Disturb him not; let him pass peaceably.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Peace to his soul, if God’s good pleasure be!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lord Cardinal, if thou think’st on heaven’s bliss,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Hold up thy hand, make signal of thy hope.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: He dies and makes no sign. O God, forgive him!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: So bad a death argues a monstrous life.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Forbear to judge, for we are sinners all.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Close up his eyes, and draw the curtain close,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And let us all to meditation.
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum. Fight at sea. Ordnance goes off. Enter a Lieutenant, Suffolk, disguised, a prisoner. The Master, a Master’s Mate, Walter Whitmore, and prisoners.

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: The gaudy, blabbing, and remorseful day

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Is crept into the bosom of the sea;

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: And now loud-howling wolves arouse the jades

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: That drag the tragic melancholy night,

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Who, with their drowsy, slow, and flagging wings

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Clip dead men’s graves and from their misty jaws

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Breathe foul contagious darkness in the air.

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Therefore bring forth the soldiers of our prize;

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: For, whilst our pinnace anchors in the Downs,

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Here shall they make their ransom on the sand,

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Or with their blood stain this discoloured shore.

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Master, this prisoner freely give I thee,

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: And thou that art his mate, make boot of this;

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: The other, Walter Whitmore, is thy share.
