lines.speaker: STAFFORD
lines.text: May, even in their wives’ and children’s sight,

lines.speaker: STAFFORD
lines.text: Be hanged up for example at their doors.

lines.speaker: STAFFORD
lines.text: And you that be the King’s friends, follow me.
[_Exeunt the two Staffords and soldiers._]

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: And you that love the commons follow me.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Now show yourselves men; ’tis for liberty.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: We will not leave one lord, one gentleman;

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Spare none but such as go in clouted shoon,

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: For they are thrifty honest men and such

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: As would, but that they dare not, take our parts.

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: They are all in order and march toward us.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: But then are we in order when we are most out of order. Come, march

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: forward.
[_Exeunt._]
[Alarums to the fight, wherein both the Staffords are slain. Enter Cade and the rest.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Where’s Dick, the butcher of Ashford?

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: Here, sir.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: They fell before thee like sheep and oxen, and thou behaved’st thyself

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: as if thou hadst been in thine own slaughterhouse. Therefore thus will

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: I reward thee: the Lent shall be as long again as it is, and thou shalt

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: have a licence to kill for a hundred lacking one.

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: I desire no more.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: And, to speak truth, thou deservest no less. This monument of the

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: victory will I bear. [_putting on Sir Humphrey’s brigandine_] And the

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: bodies shall be dragged at my horse heels till I do come to London,

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: where we will have the Mayor’s sword borne before us.

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: If we mean to thrive and do good, break open the gaols and let out the

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: prisoners.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Fear not that, I warrant thee. Come, let’s march towards London.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the King with a supplication, and the Queen with Suffolk’s head, the Duke of Buckingham and the Lord Saye.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Oft have I heard that grief softens the mind

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And makes it fearful and degenerate;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Think therefore on revenge and cease to weep.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But who can cease to weep and look on this?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Here may his head lie on my throbbing breast;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But where’s the body that I should embrace?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: What answer makes your grace to the rebels’ supplication?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I’ll send some holy bishop to entreat,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For God forbid so many simple souls

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Should perish by the sword! And I myself,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Rather than bloody war shall cut them short,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Will parley with Jack Cade their general.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But stay, I’ll read it over once again.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ah, barbarous villains! Hath this lovely face

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ruled, like a wandering planet, over me,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And could it not enforce them to relent

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That were unworthy to behold the same?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lord Saye, Jack Cade hath sworn to have thy head.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Ay, but I hope your highness shall have his.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How now, madam?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Still lamenting and mourning for Suffolk’s death?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I fear me, love, if that I had been dead,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou wouldst not have mourned so much for me.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: No, my love, I should not mourn, but die for thee.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How now, what news? Why com’st thou in such haste?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The rebels are in Southwark; fly, my lord!

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Jack Cade proclaims himself Lord Mortimer,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Descended from the Duke of Clarence’ house,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And calls your grace usurper openly,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And vows to crown himself in Westminster.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: His army is a ragged multitude

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Of hinds and peasants, rude and merciless.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Sir Humphrey Stafford and his brother’s death

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Hath given them heart and courage to proceed.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: All scholars, lawyers, courtiers, gentlemen,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: They call false caterpillars, and intend their death.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O graceless men! They know not what they do.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My gracious lord, retire to Killingworth

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Until a power be raised to put them down.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ah, were the Duke of Suffolk now alive,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: These Kentish rebels would be soon appeased!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lord Saye, the traitors hate thee;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore away with us to Killingworth.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: So might your grace’s person be in danger.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: The sight of me is odious in their eyes;

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: And therefore in this city will I stay

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: And live alone as secret as I may.
Enter another Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Jack Cade hath gotten London Bridge;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The citizens fly and forsake their houses.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The rascal people, thirsting after prey,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Join with the traitor, and they jointly swear

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To spoil the city and your royal court.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Then linger not, my lord; away, take horse!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come, Margaret. God, our hope, will succour us.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: My hope is gone, now Suffolk is deceased.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Farewell, my lord. Trust not the Kentish rebels.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Trust nobody, for fear you be betrayed.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: The trust I have is in mine innocence,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: And therefore am I bold and resolute.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Lord Scales upon the Tower, walking. Then enter two or three Citizens below.

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: How now? Is Jack Cade slain?

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: 1 CITIZEN.

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: No, my lord, nor likely to be slain; for they have won the Bridge,

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: killing all those that withstand them. The Lord Mayor craves aid of

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: your honour from the Tower to defend the city from the rebels.

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: Such aid as I can spare you shall command,

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: But I am troubled here with them myself;

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: The rebels have assayed to win the Tower.

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: But get you to Smithfield and gather head,

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: And thither I will send you Matthew Gough.

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: Fight for your king, your country, and your lives!

lines.speaker: SCALES
lines.text: And so farewell, for I must hence again.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Jack Cade and the rest, and strikes his staff on London Stone.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Now is Mortimer lord of this city. And here, sitting upon London Stone,

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: I charge and command that, of the city’s cost, the Pissing Conduit run

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: nothing but claret wine this first year of our reign. And now

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: henceforward it shall be treason for any that calls me other than Lord

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Mortimer.
Enter a Soldier, running.

lines.speaker: SOLDIER
lines.text: Jack Cade! Jack Cade!

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Knock him down there.
[_They kill him._]

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: If this fellow be wise, he’ll never call ye Jack Cade more. I think he

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: hath a very fair warning. My lord, there’s an army gathered together in

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: Smithfield.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Come then, let’s go fight with them. But first, go and set London

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Bridge on fire; and, if you can, burn down the Tower too. Come, let’s

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: away.
[_Exeunt._]
Alarums. Matthew Gough is slain, and all the rest. Then enter Jack Cade with his company.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: So, sirs. Now go some and pull down the Savoy; others to th’ Inns of

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Court; down with them all.

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: I have a suit unto your lordship.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Be it a lordship, thou shalt have it for that word.

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: Only that the laws of England may come out of your mouth.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: HOLLAND
lines.text: Mass, ’twill be sore law, then; for he was thrust in the

lines.speaker: HOLLAND
lines.text: mouth with a spear, and ’tis not whole yet.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SMITH
lines.text: Nay, John, it will be stinking law, for his breath stinks

lines.speaker: SMITH
lines.text: with eating toasted cheese.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: I have thought upon it, it shall be so. Away, burn all the records of

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: the realm. My mouth shall be the parliament of England.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: HOLLAND
lines.text: Then we are like to have biting statutes, unless his teeth

lines.speaker: HOLLAND
lines.text: be pulled out.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: And henceforward all things shall be in common.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My lord, a prize, a prize! Here’s the Lord Saye, which sold the towns

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: in France; he that made us pay one-and-twenty fifteens, and one

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: shilling to the pound, the last subsidy.
Enter George Bevis with the Lord Saye.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Well, he shall be beheaded for it ten times. Ah, thou say, thou serge,

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: nay, thou buckram lord! Now art thou within point-blank of our

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: jurisdiction regal. What canst thou answer to my majesty for giving up

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: of Normandy unto Mounsieur Basimecu, the Dauphin of France? Be it known

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: unto thee by these presence, even the presence of Lord Mortimer, that I

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: am the besom that must sweep the court clean of such filth as thou art.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Thou hast most traitorously corrupted the youth of the realm in

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: erecting a grammar school; and whereas, before, our forefathers had no

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: other books but the score and the tally, thou hast caused printing to

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: be used, and, contrary to the King, his crown, and dignity, thou hast

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: built a paper-mill. It will be proved to thy face that thou hast men

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: about thee that usually talk of a noun and a verb, and such abominable

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: words as no Christian ear can endure to hear. Thou hast appointed

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: justices of peace, to call poor men before them about matters they were

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: not able to answer. Moreover, thou hast put them in prison, and because

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: they could not read, thou hast hanged them, when indeed only for that

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: cause they have been most worthy to live. Thou dost ride on a

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: foot-cloth, dost thou not?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: What of that?

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Marry, thou ought’st not to let thy horse wear a cloak when honester

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: men than thou go in their hose and doublets.

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: And work in their shirt too; as myself, for example, that am a butcher.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: You men of Kent—

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: What say you of Kent?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Nothing but this; ’tis _bona terra, mala gens_.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Away with him, away with him! He speaks Latin.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Hear me but speak, and bear me where you will.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Kent, in the Commentaries Caesar writ,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Is termed the civil’st place of all this isle.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Sweet is the country, because full of riches;

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: The people liberal, valiant, active, wealthy;

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Which makes me hope you are not void of pity.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: I sold not Maine, I lost not Normandy,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Yet to recover them would lose my life.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Justice with favour have I always done;

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Prayers and tears have moved me, gifts could never.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: When have I aught exacted at your hands

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Kent to maintain the King, the realm, and you?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Large gifts have I bestowed on learned clerks,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Because my book preferred me to the King.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: And seeing ignorance is the curse of God,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Knowledge the wing wherewith we fly to heaven,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Unless you be possessed with devilish spirits,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: You cannot but forbear to murder me.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: This tongue hath parleyed unto foreign kings

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: For your behoof—

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Tut, when struck’st thou one blow in the field?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Great men have reaching hands; oft have I struck

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Those that I never saw, and struck them dead.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: O monstrous coward! What, to come behind folks?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: These cheeks are pale for watching for your good.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Give him a box o’ th’ ear, and that will make ’em red again.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Long sitting to determine poor men’s causes

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Hath made me full of sickness and diseases.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Ye shall have a hempen caudle then, and the help of hatchet.

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: Why dost thou quiver, man?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: The palsy, and not fear, provokes me.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Nay, he nods at us, as who should say, “I’ll be even with you.” I’ll

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: see if his head will stand steadier on a pole or no. Take him away, and

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: behead him.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Tell me, wherein have I offended most?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Have I affected wealth or honour? Speak.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Are my chests filled up with extorted gold?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Is my apparel sumptuous to behold?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Whom have I injured, that ye seek my death?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: These hands are free from guiltless bloodshedding,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: This breast from harbouring foul deceitful thoughts.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: O, let me live!
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: I feel remorse in myself with his words, but I’ll bridle it.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: He shall die, an it be but for pleading so well for his life. Away with

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: him! He has a familiar under his tongue; he speaks not i’ God’s name.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Go, take him away, I say, and strike off his head presently; and then

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: break into his son-in-law’s house, Sir James Cromer, and strike off his

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: head, and bring them both upon two poles hither.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: It shall be done.

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: Ah, countrymen, if when you make your prayers,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: God should be so obdurate as yourselves,

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: How would it fare with your departed souls?

lines.speaker: SAYE
lines.text: And therefore yet relent, and save my life.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Away with him! And do as I command ye.
[_Exeunt some with Lord Saye._]

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: The proudest peer in the realm shall not wear a head on his shoulders

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: unless he pay me tribute; there shall not a maid be married but she

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: shall pay to me her maidenhead ere they have it. Men shall hold of me

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: _in capite;_ and we charge and command that their wives be as free as

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: heart can wish or tongue can tell.

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: My lord, when shall we go to Cheapside and take up commodities upon our

lines.speaker: DICK
lines.text: bills?

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Marry, presently.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: O, brave!
Enter one with the heads.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: But is not this braver? Let them kiss one another, for they loved well

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: when they were alive. Now part them again, lest they consult about the

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: giving up of some more towns in France. Soldiers, defer the spoil of

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: the city until night; for with these borne before us instead of maces

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: will we ride through the streets, and at every corner have them kiss.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Away!
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum and retreat. Enter Cade and all his rabblement.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Up Fish Street! Down Saint Magnus’ Corner! Kill and knock down! Throw

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: them into Thames! [_Sound a parley_.] What noise is this I hear? Dare

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: any be so bold to sound retreat or parley when I command them kill?
Enter Buckingham and old Clifford attended.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Ay, here they be that dare and will disturb thee.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Know, Cade, we come ambassadors from the King

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Unto the commons, whom thou hast misled,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And here pronounce free pardon to them all

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: That will forsake thee and go home in peace.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: What say ye, countrymen? Will ye relent

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And yield to mercy whilst ’tis offered you,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Or let a rebel lead you to your deaths?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Who loves the King and will embrace his pardon,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Fling up his cap, and say “God save his Majesty!”

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Who hateth him and honours not his father,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Henry the Fifth, that made all France to quake,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Shake he his weapon at us and pass by.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: God save the King! God save the King!

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: What, Buckingham and Clifford, are ye so brave? And you, base peasants,

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: do ye believe him? Will you needs be hanged with your pardons about

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: your necks? Hath my sword therefore broke through London gates, that

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: you should leave me at the White Hart in Southwark? I thought ye would

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: never have given out these arms till you had recovered your ancient

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: freedom; but you are all recreants and dastards, and delight to live in

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: slavery to the nobility. Let them break your backs with burdens, take

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: your houses over your heads, ravish your wives and daughters before

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: your faces. For me, I will make shift for one, and so God’s curse light

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: upon you all!

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: We’ll follow Cade! We’ll follow Cade!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Is Cade the son of Henry the Fifth,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: That thus you do exclaim you’ll go with him?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Will he conduct you through the heart of France

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And make the meanest of you earls and dukes?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Alas, he hath no home, no place to fly to,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Nor knows he how to live but by the spoil,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Unless by robbing of your friends and us.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Were ’t not a shame that whilst you live at jar

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: The fearful French, whom you late vanquished,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Should make a start o’er seas and vanquish you?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Methinks already in this civil broil

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: I see them lording it in London streets,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Crying “_Villiago!_” unto all they meet.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Better ten thousand base-born Cades miscarry

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Than you should stoop unto a Frenchman’s mercy.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: To France, to France, and get what you have lost!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Spare England, for it is your native coast.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Henry hath money, you are strong and manly;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: God on our side, doubt not of victory.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: A Clifford! A Clifford! We’ll follow the King and Clifford.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Was ever feather so lightly blown to and fro as this multitude? The

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: name of Henry the Fifth hales them to an hundred mischiefs and makes

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: them leave me desolate. I see them lay their heads together to surprise

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: me. My sword make way for me, for here is no staying.—In despite of the

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: devils and hell, have through the very middest of you! And heavens and

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: honour be witness that no want of resolution in me, but only my

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: followers’ base and ignominious treasons, makes me betake me to my

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: heels.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: What, is he fled? Go some, and follow him;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And he that brings his head unto the King

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Shall have a thousand crowns for his reward.
[_Exeunt some of them._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Follow me, soldiers; we’ll devise a mean

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To reconcile you all unto the King.
[_Exeunt._]
Sound trumpets. Enter King, Queen and Somerset on the terrace, aloft.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Was ever king that joyed an earthly throne

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And could command no more content than I?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No sooner was I crept out of my cradle

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But I was made a king at nine months old.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Was never subject longed to be a king

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As I do long and wish to be a subject.
Enter Buckingham and old Clifford.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Health and glad tidings to your majesty!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, Buckingham, is the traitor Cade surprised?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or is he but retired to make him strong?
Enter below multitudes with halters about their necks.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: He is fled, my lord, and all his powers do yield,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And humbly thus, with halters on their necks,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Expect your highness’ doom of life or death.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then, heaven, set ope thy everlasting gates

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To entertain my vows of thanks and praise!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Soldiers, this day have you redeemed your lives

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And showed how well you love your prince and country.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Continue still in this so good a mind,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And Henry, though he be infortunate,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Assure yourselves, will never be unkind.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And so, with thanks and pardon to you all,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I do dismiss you to your several countries.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: God save the King! God save the King!
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Please it your grace to be advertised

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Duke of York is newly come from Ireland,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And with a puissant and a mighty power

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Of gallowglasses and stout kerns

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Is marching hitherward in proud array,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And still proclaimeth, as he comes along,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: His arms are only to remove from thee

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Duke of Somerset, whom he terms a traitor.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thus stands my state, ’twixt Cade and York distressed,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Like to a ship that, having scaped a tempest,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Is straightway calmed and boarded with a pirate.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But now is Cade driven back, his men dispersed,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And now is York in arms to second him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I pray thee, Buckingham, go and meet him,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And ask him what’s the reason of these arms.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tell him I’ll send Duke Edmund to the Tower.—

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, Somerset, we will commit thee thither,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Until his army be dismissed from him.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: My lord, I’ll yield myself to prison willingly,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Or unto death, to do my country good.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: In any case, be not too rough in terms,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For he is fierce and cannot brook hard language.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I will, my lord, and doubt not so to deal

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: As all things shall redound unto your good.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come, wife, let’s in, and learn to govern better;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For yet may England curse my wretched reign.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]
Enter Cade.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Fie on ambitions! Fie on myself, that have a sword and yet am ready to

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: famish! These five days have I hid me in these woods and durst not peep

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: out, for all the country is laid for me; but now am I so hungry that if

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: I might have a lease of my life for a thousand years, I could stay no

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: longer. Wherefore, o’er a brick wall have I climbed into this garden,

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: to see if I can eat grass, or pick a sallet another while, which is not

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: amiss to cool a man’s stomach this hot weather. And I think this word

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: “sallet” was born to do me good; for many a time, but for a sallet, my

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: brain-pan had been cleft with a brown bill; and many a time, when I

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: have been dry and bravely marching, it hath served me instead of a

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: quart pot to drink in; and now the word “sallet” must serve me to feed

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: on.
Enter Iden and his men.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Lord, who would live turmoiled in the court

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: And may enjoy such quiet walks as these?

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: This small inheritance my father left me

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Contenteth me, and worth a monarchy.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: I seek not to wax great by others’ waning,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Or gather wealth, I care not with what envy;

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Sufficeth that I have maintains my state

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: And sends the poor well pleased from my gate.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Here’s the lord of the soil come to seize me for a stray, for entering

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: his fee-simple without leave.—Ah, villain, thou wilt betray me and get

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: a thousand crowns of the King by carrying my head to him; but I’ll make

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: thee eat iron like an ostrich, and swallow my sword like a great pin,

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: ere thou and I part.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Why, rude companion, whatsoe’er thou be,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: I know thee not; why, then, should I betray thee?

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Is ’t not enough to break into my garden

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: And, like a thief, to come to rob my grounds,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Climbing my walls in spite of me the owner,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: But thou wilt brave me with these saucy terms?

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Brave thee? Ay, by the best blood that ever was broached, and beard

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: thee too. Look on me well: I have eat no meat these five days, yet come

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: thou and thy five men, and if I do not leave you all as dead as a

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: doornail, I pray God I may never eat grass more.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Nay, it shall ne’er be said, while England stands,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: That Alexander Iden, an esquire of Kent,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Took odds to combat a poor famished man.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Oppose thy steadfast-gazing eyes to mine,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: See if thou canst outface me with thy looks.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Set limb to limb and thou art far the lesser;

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Thy hand is but a finger to my fist,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Thy leg a stick compared with this truncheon.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: My foot shall fight with all the strength thou hast;

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: And if mine arm be heaved in the air,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Thy grave is digged already in the earth.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: As for words, whose greatness answers words,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Let this my sword report what speech forbears.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: By my valour, the most complete champion that ever I heard! Steel, if

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: thou turn the edge, or cut not out the burly-boned clown in chines of

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: beef ere thou sleep in thy sheath, I beseech God on my knees thou mayst

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: be turned to hobnails.
[_Here they fight and Cade falls._]

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: O, I am slain! Famine and no other hath slain me. Let ten thousand

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: devils come against me, and give me but the ten meals I have lost, and

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: I’d defy them all. Wither, garden; and be henceforth a burying place to

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: all that do dwell in this house, because the unconquered soul of Cade

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: is fled.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Is’t Cade that I have slain, that monstrous traitor?

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Sword, I will hallow thee for this thy deed,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: And hang thee o’er my tomb when I am dead.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Ne’er shall this blood be wiped from thy point,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: But thou shalt wear it as a herald’s coat

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: To emblaze the honour that thy master got.

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: Iden, farewell, and be proud of thy victory. Tell Kent from me she hath

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: lost her best man, and exhort all the world to be cowards; for I, that

lines.speaker: CADE
lines.text: never feared any, am vanquished by famine, not by valour.
[_Dies._]

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: How much thou wrong’st me, heaven be my judge.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Die, damned wretch, the curse of her that bare thee!

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: And as I thrust thy body in with my sword,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: So wish I, I might thrust thy soul to hell.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Hence will I drag thee headlong by the heels

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Unto a dunghill, which shall be thy grave,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: And there cut off thy most ungracious head,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Which I will bear in triumph to the King,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Leaving thy trunk for crows to feed upon.
[_Exit._]
Enter York and his army of Irish, with drum and colours.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: From Ireland thus comes York to claim his right

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And pluck the crown from feeble Henry’s head.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Ring, bells, aloud; burn, bonfires, clear and bright,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To entertain great England’s lawful king.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Ah, _sancta majestas_, who would not buy thee dear?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Let them obey that knows not how to rule.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: This hand was made to handle nought but gold.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I cannot give due action to my words

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Except a sword or sceptre balance it.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: A sceptre shall it have, have I a soul,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: On which I’ll toss the fleur-de-luce of France.
Enter Buckingham.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whom have we here? Buckingham, to disturb me?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The King hath sent him, sure. I must dissemble.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: York, if thou meanest well, I greet thee well.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Humphrey of Buckingham, I accept thy greeting.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Art thou a messenger, or come of pleasure?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: A messenger from Henry, our dread liege,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To know the reason of these arms in peace;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Or why thou, being a subject as I am,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Against thy oath and true allegiance sworn,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Should raise so great a power without his leave,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Or dare to bring thy force so near the court.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Scarce can I speak, my choler is so great.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: O, I could hew up rocks and fight with flint,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I am so angry at these abject terms;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And now, like Ajax Telamonius,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: On sheep or oxen could I spend my fury.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I am far better born than is the King,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: More like a king, more kingly in my thoughts.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But I must make fair weather yet awhile,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Till Henry be more weak and I more strong.—

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Buckingham, I prithee, pardon me,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That I have given no answer all this while;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My mind was troubled with deep melancholy.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The cause why I have brought this army hither

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Is to remove proud Somerset from the King,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Seditious to his grace and to the state.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: That is too much presumption on thy part;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But if thy arms be to no other end,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The King hath yielded unto thy demand:

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The Duke of Somerset is in the Tower.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Upon thine honour, is he prisoner?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Upon mine honour, he is prisoner.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then, Buckingham, I do dismiss my powers.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Soldiers, I thank you all; disperse yourselves;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Meet me tomorrow in Saint George’s field,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: You shall have pay and everything you wish.
[_Exeunt Soldiers._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And let my sovereign, virtuous Henry,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Command my eldest son, nay, all my sons,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: As pledges of my fealty and love,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I’ll send them all as willing as I live.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Lands, goods, horse, armour, anything I have

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Is his to use, so Somerset may die.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: York, I commend this kind submission.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: We twain will go into his highness’ tent.
Enter King and Attendants.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Buckingham, doth York intend no harm to us

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That thus he marcheth with thee arm in arm?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In all submission and humility

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: York doth present himself unto your highness.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then what intends these forces thou dost bring?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To heave the traitor Somerset from hence

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And fight against that monstrous rebel Cade,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Who since I heard to be discomfited.
Enter Iden with Cade’s head.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: If one so rude and of so mean condition

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: May pass into the presence of a king,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Lo, I present your grace a traitor’s head,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: The head of Cade, whom I in combat slew.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The head of Cade! Great God, how just art Thou!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O, let me view his visage, being dead,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That living wrought me such exceeding trouble.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tell me, my friend, art thou the man that slew him?

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: I was, an ’t like your majesty.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How art thou called? And what is thy degree?

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: Alexander Iden, that’s my name;

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: A poor esquire of Kent, that loves his King.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: So please it you, my lord, ’twere not amiss

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: He were created knight for his good service.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Iden, kneel down. [_He kneels_.] Rise up a knight.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We give thee for reward a thousand marks,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And will that thou henceforth attend on us.

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: May Iden live to merit such a bounty,

lines.speaker: IDEN
lines.text: And never live but true unto his liege!
[_Rises._]
Enter Queen and Somerset.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: See, Buckingham, Somerset comes with the Queen.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go, bid her hide him quickly from the Duke.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For thousand Yorks he shall not hide his head,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But boldly stand and front him to his face.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: How now? Is Somerset at liberty?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then, York, unloose thy long-imprisoned thoughts,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And let thy tongue be equal with thy heart.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Shall I endure the sight of Somerset?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: False king, why hast thou broken faith with me,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Knowing how hardly I can brook abuse?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: “King” did I call thee? No, thou art not king,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Not fit to govern and rule multitudes,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Which dar’st not, no, nor canst not rule a traitor.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That head of thine doth not become a crown;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Thy hand is made to grasp a palmer’s staff,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And not to grace an awful princely sceptre.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That gold must round engirt these brows of mine,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whose smile and frown, like to Achilles’ spear,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Is able with the change to kill and cure.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Here is a hand to hold a sceptre up

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And with the same to act controlling laws.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Give place! By heaven, thou shalt rule no more

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: O’er him whom heaven created for thy ruler.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: O monstrous traitor! I arrest thee, York,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Of capital treason ’gainst the King and crown.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Obey, audacious traitor, kneel for grace.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Wouldst have me kneel? First let me ask of these

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: If they can brook I bow a knee to man.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Sirrah, call in my sons to be my bail.
[_Exit Attendant._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I know, ere they will have me go to ward,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: They’ll pawn their swords for my enfranchisement.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Call hither Clifford; bid him come amain,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To say if that the bastard boys of York

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Shall be the surety for their traitor father.
[_Exit Buckingham._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: O blood-bespotted Neapolitan,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Outcast of Naples, England’s bloody scourge!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The sons of York, thy betters in their birth,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Shall be their father’s bail; and bane to those

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That for my surety will refuse the boys!
Enter Edward and Richard.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: See where they come; I’ll warrant they’ll make it good.
Enter old Clifford and his Son.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And here comes Clifford to deny their bail.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Health and all happiness to my lord the King.
[_Rises._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I thank thee, Clifford. Say, what news with thee?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Nay, do not fright us with an angry look.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: We are thy sovereign, Clifford, kneel again.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For thy mistaking so, we pardon thee.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: This is my king, York, I do not mistake;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: But thou mistakes me much to think I do.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: To Bedlam with him! Is the man grown mad?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, Clifford; a bedlam and ambitious humour

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Makes him oppose himself against his king.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: He is a traitor; let him to the Tower,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And chop away that factious pate of his.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: He is arrested, but will not obey;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His sons, he says, shall give their words for him.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Will you not, sons?

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Ay, noble father, if our words will serve.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And if words will not, then our weapons shall.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Why, what a brood of traitors have we here!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Look in a glass, and call thy image so.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I am thy king, and thou a false-heart traitor.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Call hither to the stake my two brave bears,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That with the very shaking of their chains

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: They may astonish these fell-lurking curs.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Bid Salisbury and Warwick come to me.
Enter the Earls of Warwick and Salisbury.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Are these thy bears? We’ll bait thy bears to death

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And manacle the bearherd in their chains,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: If thou dar’st bring them to the baiting-place.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Oft have I seen a hot o’erweening cur

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Run back and bite because he was withheld,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Who, being suffered with the bear’s fell paw,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Hath clapped his tail between his legs and cried;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And such a piece of service will you do

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If you oppose yourselves to match Lord Warwick.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Hence, heap of wrath, foul indigested lump,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: As crooked in thy manners as thy shape!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Nay, we shall heat you thoroughly anon.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Take heed, lest by your heat you burn yourselves.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, Warwick, hath thy knee forgot to bow?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Old Salisbury, shame to thy silver hair,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou mad misleader of thy brainsick son!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
